assessments.reasoning: For the stipulated defined type, receiver T places a declared method in both method sets. Receiver *T places it only in the pointer’s set. The specification gives embedded fields and interfaces separate treatment.

challenge.method: Consider a pointer-receiver method accessible through an addressable variable of type T. Does that call put the method in T’s set for interface satisfaction?
challenge.results: No. The membership rule still assigns that declaration only to *T. Call syntax supplies no additional member of T’s set.

limitations: Separate rules govern promoted methods and calling a method with an implicit address-of operation.
The conclusion covers declared methods and the specified receiver base. Promotion and implicit address-taking have separate rules.
